law.label: Law (قانون / Loi)

hierarchy.note: Major codes only (Penal Code, Code of Obligations and Contracts). Rare in standalone laws.
Primary structural grouping. Maps to AKN title (not chapter). باب الأول, Titre I.
Sub-grouping below Bab/Titre. الفصل الأول, Chapitre I.
Section as HIGHER division above articles. Bluebell workaround: DIVISION keyword; post-process <division> → <section>. قسم is a higher division, not the basic unit.
THE basic citable unit. Numbered continuously throughout the entire law regardless of higher division boundaries. Never restarts per Bab or Fasl.
Paragraph break within an article. Usually unnumbered. Some modern laws use (1), (2). Post-process: <paragraph> → <alinea>.
Lettered or numbered list items within an alinéa: (أ), (ب), (ج) or (a), (b), (c) or 1., 2., 3.

law.note: Standard parliamentary law (قانون). Article is always the basic unit. Most standalone laws use only Bab/Titre > Article; larger laws and codes add Fasl/Chapitre and Qism/Section. Article numbering is continuous throughout regardless of higher divisions.

legislative_decree.label: Legislative Decree (مرسوم تشريعي / Décret législatif)
legislative_decree.note: Executive legislation enacted when Parliament is suspended or during Mandate period. Structurally identical to ordinary laws. Distinguished by enacting formula (President/Council of Ministers, not Chamber of Deputies) and FRBR subtype 'legislative-decree'. Includes major codes: Penal Code (No. 340/1943), Code of Criminal Procedure.

decree_law.label: Decree-Law (مرسوم بقوة القانون)
decree_law.note: Emergency executive legislation issued by the President and Council of Ministers under special constitutional circumstances. Requires subsequent parliamentary ratification to remain in force. Structurally identical to ordinary laws.

decree.label: Decree (مرسوم / Décret)
decree.note: Regulatory/administrative decrees (not primary legislation). Signed by President and countersigned by relevant minister(s). Very high sequential numbers (e.g., Decree No. 11230). Typically short — mostly just articles. Published in Al-Jarida Al-Rasmiyya.

personal_status.label: Personal Status Law (قانون الأحوال الشخصية)

hcontainers.name: proviso
hcontainers.description: Proviso or conditional note attached to an article, sometimes with independent legal force in confessional court practice

personal_status.note: Applies to Parliament-ratified personal status instruments for Lebanon's 18 recognised religious communities. Structural terminology varies by community: Islamic courts use Arabic jurisprudential terms; Christian communities may use Latin canon law terms (Titulus, Canon) or their Arabic/French equivalents. Model each community's instruments using the closest AKN mapping. See profile.md for the full list of 18 communities and their court systems.

constitution.label: Constitution (الدستور / Constitution)

hierarchy.note: Articles 1–102 (as amended through 1990 Taif). No higher structural divisions in the constitution itself beyond the Preamble/Body distinction.

hcontainers.name: preamble
hcontainers.description: Constitutional Preamble added by Taif Agreement amendments (1990). Distinct constitutional status — part of the constitutional bloc (bloc de constitutionnalité). Not a simple introductory paragraph. Model as hcontainer within preface.

constitution.note: Constitution of 23 May 1926 (as amended through 1990 Taif Agreement). 102 articles, no higher structural divisions within the body. The 1990 preamble has full constitutional force per Constitutional Council jurisprudence. Each amendment round is a separate FRBR expression of the 1926 work.

frbr.note: Law number taken from 'Law No. {number}/{year}' citation. Arabic-Indic numerals (١-٩) in source documents must be normalised to Western Arabic (1-9) for URI construction. For laws cited by date only (pre-numbering era), use slugified subject descriptor as number segment. Ottoman-era laws still in force receive URIs under lb/act/ottoman/ with metadata noting original Ottoman provenance.

numbering.note: Insertion style inconsistent across eras and drafters. Mandate-era and French-tradition instruments use hyphen suffix (-1, -2); Arabic-tradition instruments use mكرراً (mkarran/bis). Detect per document and record in metadata.

enacting_formulae.arabic:
رئيس الجمهورية،
بناءً على الدستور، لا سيما المواد 17 و51 منه،
وبناءً على قرار مجلس النواب بتاريخ {date}،
يصدر القانون الآتي نصه:
enacting_formulae.french:
Le Président de la République,
Vu la Constitution, et notamment ses articles 17 et 51,
Vu la décision de la Chambre des Députés en date du {date},
Promulgue la loi dont la teneur suit :
enacting_formulae.note: Standard post-independence promulgation formula. Countersigned by Prime Minister and relevant minister(s). Arabic is authoritative; French text also appears in Official Gazette.

enacting_formulae.french:
Le Gouvernement de la République libanaise,
Vu la Constitution,
[VISA block]
Arrête :
enacting_formulae.arabic:
حكومة الجمهورية اللبنانية،
bناءً على الدستور،
[بلوك الإشارات]
تقرر ما يأتي:
enacting_formulae.note: Used for مراسيم تشريعية (legislative decrees) issued by Council of Ministers when Parliament is not in session. The VISA block references constitutional authorization. 'Arrête'/'تقرر' is the decision verb.

enacting_formulae.french:
Nous, [Name], Président de la République Libanaise,
Vu la Constitution,
[VISA block]
Décrétons :
enacting_formulae.note: French Mandate-era formula. French only; Arabic translation sometimes appended. 'Décrétons' is the enacting verb. These instruments are legislative decrees with French sole authorship.

amendments.phrasing_substitution_arabic: يُعدَّل المادة {N} من القانون رقم {number} تاريخ {date} وفق ما يلي:
amendments.phrasing_repeal_arabic: تُلغى المادة {N} من القانون رقم {number} تاريخ {date}
amendments.phrasing_addition_arabic: يُضاف إلى القانون رقم {number} مادة جديدة رقمها {N مكرراً} تنص على ما يلي:
amendments.phrasing_substitution_french: L'article {N} de la loi n° {number} est modifié comme suit :
amendments.phrasing_repeal_french: L'article {N} de la loi n° {number} est abrogé.

core_tlcs.showAs: Speaker of the Chamber of Deputies

structuring.prompt_additions: Lebanon uses Arabic (authoritative) and French (working language). Basic unit is ARTICLE (مادة/Maddah) — never SECTION. Hierarchy for major codes and laws: [BOOK >] TITLE > CHAPTER > [DIVISION >] ARTICLE. Simple laws: [TITLE >] [CHAPTER >] ARTICLE only. DIVISION keyword maps to قسم/Section (a higher division above articles, NOT the basic unit); post-process <division> → <section> in output. PARAGRAPH maps to فقرة/Alinéa (paragraph break within an article, usually unnumbered); post-process <paragraph> → <alinea>. POINT maps to بند/point (lettered or numbered list item). Article numbering is continuous throughout the entire law regardless of TITLE or CHAPTER boundaries — never restart the count. Arabic-Indic numerals (١-٩) must be normalised to Western Arabic (1-9) in structural positions. Use ASCII Bluebell keywords (ARTICLE, TITLE, CHAPTER, etc.) but preserve Arabic and French article body text verbatim. Insertion articles: مادة 5 مكرراً → ARTICLE 5mkarran; Article 5-1 → ARTICLE 5-1. RTL text direction required for Arabic content.

supranational_memberships.note: Lebanon is a founding Arab League member (1945). League conventions require domestic ratification; no direct effect comparable to EU Regulations.

direct_effect_exceptions: Security Council Chapter VII resolutions — binding in international law
supranational_memberships.note: Lebanon hosts UNIFIL (UN Interim Force in Lebanon) under Chapter VI/VII mandates. Extensive UN Security Council engagement on Lebanon.
Lebanon acceded to WTO 1999. TRIPS obligations incorporated into domestic IP law (Laws No. 75/1999, No. 240/2000).

display.note: Arabic RTL primary display. French text may appear alongside Arabic in gazette publications; Arabic is authoritative. Article headings in Arabic legislation often appear as bold inline text at the start of the article or as a rubric above it. Review UI must support RTL (direction: rtl; unicode-bidi: embed) for Arabic content, with LTR override for structural keywords and numbering.
